title: Fabricating Sale Agreements, Selling Property in Breach of a Court Undertaking Warrants Prosecution: AP High Court
case_name: Thota Gopal & Others v. Pandipati Gopal Reddy & Others
card_summary: A Division Bench dismissed appeals in a 2007 specific performance dispute, finding the defendants had fabricated rival sale agreements to defeat the plaintiff's claim. It also found that despite an undertaking not to alienate the land during the appeals, the owners sold it in December 2022, and directed the Registrar to lodge complaints for perjury and fraudulent transfer under Sections 193 and 206 IPC.
card_tip: An undertaking not to alienate suit property during an appeal is not a formality; selling in breach of it can expose a party to criminal prosecution under Section 206 IPC in addition to losing the civil appeal.
verification_notes: LiveLaw and SupremeToday.ai both report the same bench, the fabricated sale agreements, the December 2022 sale deeds executed despite the undertaking, and the direction to prosecute under Sections 193 and 206 IPC. SupremeToday.ai also reports the agreements were ante-dated (stamp papers issued after the agreement date) and that the underlying suit concerned over 31 acres. Neither report states an exact pronouncement date; decision_date is inferred from the reports' publication dates (21 October 2026) and LiveLaw's weekly round-up window of 19-25 October 2026, which falls within the scope window either way. Both reports are secondary summaries of a paywalled LiveLaw report; the full judgment was not independently reviewed.
